sections.title: What Ethernet Is
sections.body: Ethernet is THE Layer-2 technology used in almost every wired LAN today. It defines how devices format data (frames), how they are addressed (MAC), and how they take turns on the wire.

sections.title: FCS — The Integrity Check
sections.body: Sender calculates a number from the frame contents and puts it in FCS. Receiver recalculates; if it differs, the frame was damaged in transit and is silently dropped. Ethernet does NOT resend — that is TCPs job if needed.

sections.title: Size Rules
points: Payload limit = 1500 bytes — the famous MTU.
Too small ("runt") or too big ("giant") = discarded.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: MTU 1500 lives at Layer 2 with Ethernet.
